::: {.lead}
Today you finish your course project: the final versions of the three
files, and one AI-use statement for the whole project. There are no new
ideas: you use what you learned in Lectures 6–20. **Part A** is your own
project in Excel, Word and PowerPoint on the lab computer; **Part B** is
on a simulator of the interactive page: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Excel, Word and PowerPoint, your three
  files from Practices 8 and 9 (`project.xlsx`, `report.docx`,
  `talk.pptx`), and an AI assistant that the university allows (for
  example `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Office.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · The final data sheet

**The idea (Lectures 11, 13, 19 and 20):** one clean **table**: one row
for each record, no empty rows, the same spelling in each column. A
**formula** column and a total row. A **PivotTable** for the summary:
after a change in the table, **Refresh** it. **One chart** that answers
your question, with a title that says what it shows: columns compare, a
line shows a change over time.

**Aim:** finish the data sheet of your project.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Excel)**
:::

1. Open `project.xlsx`. Check the table: no empty rows, no row typed
   twice, the same spelling in each column. Correct what is wrong, then
   click the PivotTable › **PivotTable Analyze › Refresh**.

   {{< record "What I corrected … ; Grand Total … ; total row …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   After Refresh, the **Grand Total equals the total row** of the table.
   If not, the PivotTable misses rows: check that the table has all the
   rows, then refresh again.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You corrected a number in the table. What do you do to the PivotTable?

   - [x] Refresh it.

     Why: A PivotTable does not change by itself.

   - [ ] Nothing: it changes by itself.

     Why: It changes only when you refresh it.

   - [ ] Delete it and make a new one.

     Why: Refresh is enough.
   :::

2. Check your chart: is it the right chart for your question, and does its
   title say what it shows? Correct it if needed, and save the file.

   {{< record "My chart … ; its title …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Compare items or subjects: a **column chart**; a change over the days
   or the weeks: a **line chart**. A good title, for example "Minutes of
   study by subject (two weeks)", never "Chart Title".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Your question asks how your study minutes changed over two weeks. Which
   chart answers it?

   - [x] a line chart of the minutes per day

     Why: A line shows a change over time.

   - [ ] a pie chart of the days

     Why: A pie shows the parts of one whole, not a change.

   - [ ] a column chart of the subjects

     Why: It compares the subjects, not the change over the days.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-07/sims/chart-lab.html" poster="../../week-07/sims/chart-lab.png" title="Chart Lab: the right chart for the question" >}}

3. In **Chart Lab**, do Task 1: compare the three types with a column
   chart, and give it a real title. Which title did you write?

   {{< record "My title …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A title that says what the chart shows, for example "Sales per type in
   one week (JD)". "Chart Title" does not pass the task.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which title is good for the chart of the canteen?

   - [x] Total by item in four weeks (JD)

     Why: A good title says what the chart shows.

   - [ ] Chart 1

     Why: It says nothing about the numbers.

   - [ ] My chart

     Why: It does not say what the chart shows.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · The final report

**The idea (Lectures 7, 8, 9 and 19):** keep the five headings (Heading
1). If a number changed in Excel, copy the chart again and paste it over
the old one, then check every number of the text against Excel. Check
every AI sentence: true, shown by the data, and in your own words. Add a
**table of contents** (**References › Table of Contents**) and **page
numbers** (**Insert › Page Number**).

**Aim:** finish the report of your project.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Open `report.docx`. Click under the title and choose **References ›
   Table of Contents** › the first automatic table. Then choose **Insert ›
   Page Number › Bottom of Page**, and a number in the middle.

   {{< record "My table of contents shows …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The **five headings with their page numbers**: Word makes the contents
   from the Heading 1 styles. After a change of the headings, click
   **Update Table**.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You add a heading after you made the table of contents. What do you do?

   - [x] Click Update Table.

     Why: The table of contents does not change by itself.

   - [ ] Type the heading into the contents by hand.

     Why: Word makes the contents; update it instead.

   - [ ] Nothing: it changes by itself.

     Why: It changes only when you update it.
   :::

2. Check every number of the text against Excel, and every AI sentence.
   Under *What I learned*, write one change that you made after your
   rehearsal or your talk.

   {{< record "What I corrected … ; my change after the talk …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Every number of the report is as in your PivotTable; an AI sentence
   that the data does not show is corrected or deleted. A good change, for
   example: "After my rehearsal, I cut one sentence on each slide and said
   my main insight first."
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   An AI sentence says "I studied Maths the most." Your PivotTable says
   English, 230 minutes. What do you do?

   - [x] Correct it with the number from Excel.

     Why: Every AI sentence is checked against your data.

   - [ ] Keep it: it sounds right.

     Why: The data shows English, not Maths.

   - [ ] Delete the whole part Results.

     Why: Correct the wrong sentence; keep the rest.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-04/sims/toc-builder.html" poster="../../week-04/sims/toc-builder.png" title="Contents Builder: headings, contents, update" >}}

3. In **Contents Builder**, give each heading its style, and insert the
   contents. On which page is *Conclusion*? Then change a heading: what do
   you press?

   {{< record "Conclusion: page … ; after a change: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Page 4**. After a change, press **Update Table**: the contents do not
   change by themselves.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which lines does Word put in the table of contents?

   - [x] the lines with a heading style

     Why: Word makes the contents from the heading styles.

   - [ ] every line in bold

     Why: Bold is not a heading style.

   - [ ] the first line of each page

     Why: The pages do not decide; the styles do.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · The final slides and the AI-use statement

**The idea (Lectures 15, 17 and 18):** after your changes, use the **four
checks** again on every slide: accuracy, claims, pictures, honesty. Keep
five slides with speaker notes. Write one **AI-use statement** for the
whole project: the tool, what it did, what you changed and how you
checked it. It goes at the end of the report (under *AI use*), with a
short AI-use line on slide 5. No personal data in any file or prompt.

**Aim:** finish the slides, and state the AI use of the whole project.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (PowerPoint and Word)**
:::

1. Open `talk.pptx`. Check every slide again with the four checks, and
   change every number that changed in Excel. Save it.

   {{< record "What I changed on the slides …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Accuracy** first: every number on a slide is as in the final Excel.
   Five slides with speaker notes, and an AI-use line on slide 5.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You changed a total in Excel after the talk. Which check do you do
   again on the slides?

   - [x] accuracy

     Why: Every number on a slide must be the same as in Excel.

   - [ ] pictures

     Why: The pictures did not change.

   - [ ] honesty

     Why: Honesty is about the AI use, not the numbers.
   :::

2. Under *AI use* in `report.docx`, write your AI-use statement for the
   whole project in three to five sentences. Put a short AI-use line on
   slide 5 too.

   {{< record "My statement" lines=3 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   For example: "I used Microsoft Copilot for ideas and a first draft of
   two sentences of the Results. I sent it no personal data. I checked
   every number with my PivotTable, corrected one wrong total, and wrote
   the text in my own words." It names the tool, the use, the changes and
   the checks.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A statement says only "AI was used." What is missing?

   - [x] for what, what you changed and how you checked it

     Why: The four parts show which work is your own.

   - [ ] the colour of the text

     Why: The look does not make a statement honest.

   - [ ] nothing: it is enough

     Why: It does not say what the AI did or what you checked.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-12/sims/statement-builder.html" poster="../../week-12/sims/statement-builder.png" title="Statement Builder: say how you used AI" >}}

3. In **Statement Builder**, do Task 3: make all five checks green. Which
   change and which check did you choose?

   {{< record "The change … ; the check …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   For example **"I rewrote it in my own words"** and **"I checked every
   fact in two reliable sources"**, with the tool and its uses. "I kept
   the text as it was" and "I did not check it" stay red.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Where does the AI-use statement of the project go?

   - [x] at the end of the report, and a short line on slide 5

     Why: Readers and listeners both see where AI helped.

   - [ ] only in an e-mail to the teacher

     Why: The statement belongs to the work itself.

   - [ ] nowhere, if the teacher does not ask

     Why: Honest work always says when AI helped.
   :::
